title: Quarterly Runway: Hosted API Demand Forecasting + Model Rotation Playbook
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the Q2 quarterly playbook to align Hosted API capacity forecasting with the model catalog rotation schedule. The goal is to produce a run-ready calendar and operational playbook that: (1) forecasts demand per endpoint/model by cadence buckets (baseline, growth, event-driven spikes), (2) prescribes hedging capacity (dedicated vs burst) and fallback model tiers, and (3) defines canary windows, metrics, and rollback criteria tied to the model catalog release process.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Produce a three-month demand forecast with 80% confidence intervals for top 25 endpoints (by revenue and latency sensitivity).
- Define canary gates: latency, p99 tail, generation quality (eval set pass rate), and token-unit cost delta thresholds.
- Ship a calendar with canary windows and a pre-approved fallback mapping (model variant -> fallback variant) for the next quarter.
- Integrate canary metrics into a Console dashboard and create alert runbooks for automatic rollback.

Scope in this ticket:
- Forecasting methodology (historical smoothing, seasonality, one-off event tagging).
- Canary calendar and flighting policy for Hosted API model swaps (including variant compatibility matrix).
- Playbook content (owner, pre-checklist, rollback steps, stakeholder notification template).

Out of scope:
- Implementation of autoscaling engine changes (tracked in ENG-1983).
- Changes to pricing model or billing signals.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Conservative hedging (reserve dedicated capacity) vs. cost-optimized burst reliance. We recommend a hybrid: reserve 60% of expected base, allow burst for 40% with pre-authorized capacity pools.
- Long canary windows increase confidence but slow rollout cadence; propose staggered short canaries with more telemetry-driven gating.

Deliverables:
- Demand forecast spreadsheet and assumptions (CSV attached in links).
- Canary calendar (ICS export) + stakeholder notification templates.
- Playbook doc (Confluence) and Console dashboard wireframe.

Owners and approvers:
- PM owner: Marcus Lee
- Eng owners: Elena Park (runtime), Jonah Reyes (autoscale)
- Design/Docs: Sophie Grant

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Week 1: finalize forecast, publish draft playbook, review with runtime and SRE.
2) Week 2: prototype canary dashboard, run single simulated swap on staging with telemetry capture.
3) Week 3: execute a low-risk live canary using non-critical model variant; evaluate against gates.
4) Week 4: iterate and finalize calendar; handoff to Ops for Q2 execution.

Risks and mitigations:
- Forecast misses due to marketing-driven spikes: require 72h pre-notification window for large marketing events and an 'event spike' override lane.
- Canary telemetry insufficient: add synthetic traffic tests scheduled into canary windows.
